title: Software developer
summary: Turn an idea into an app, website or system that helps people do something better.
tasks: Understand a user’s problem and plan a solution.
Write, review and test software with a team.
Improve a product after people start using it.
route: Explore computing or a related degree, build a portfolio of projects, and investigate internships. Entry routes differ by employer.
activity: Sketch an app that solves one problem at school. Draw three screens, then build one in Scratch or HTML.
question: What would you build if you could solve one everyday frustration?

title: Registered nurse
summary: Support people through illness and recovery, combining science with careful, compassionate care.
tasks: Monitor a patient’s condition and keep accurate records.
Deliver care and coordinate with other healthcare professionals.
Help patients and families understand their care.
route: Investigate an approved nursing programme, supervised clinical learning and the registration or licensing rules where you want to work.
activity: Create a plain-language poster explaining the importance of handwashing, using a trusted public-health source.
question: How would you help someone feel heard when they are worried?

title: Graphic designer
summary: Use images, colour and typography to make a message clear, memorable and engaging.
tasks: Understand the message and audience behind a brief.
Develop layouts, illustrations and visual identities.
Present ideas and refine designs after feedback.
route: Explore design education and build a portfolio showing how you develop and improve ideas. Learn the tools used in the kind of design you enjoy.
activity: Design two posters for the same school event: one for younger students and one for parents.
question: How would your design change when the audience changes?

title: Civil engineer
summary: Help shape the places we live, from bridges and roads to water systems and buildings.
tasks: Study a site, drawings and project constraints.
Develop designs and review materials or costs.
Coordinate construction work and check project standards.
route: Explore civil engineering study, practical placements and any professional registration needed for your intended role and country.
activity: Build two paper bridges with the same amount of paper. Compare how their shapes affect the number of coins they can support.
question: Which design used its materials most effectively, and why?

title: Secondary school teacher
summary: Help young people understand a subject, grow in confidence and discover what they can do.
tasks: Plan lessons around what students need to learn.
Teach, ask questions and adapt explanations.
Review work and give feedback that helps students improve.
route: Investigate a subject or education degree, teacher training and supervised classroom experience. Check local certification requirements.
activity: Teach a friend one idea in five minutes. Ask them to explain it back, then improve your explanation.
question: How do you know whether someone has understood you?

title: Accountant
summary: Make sense of financial records so people and organisations can make informed decisions.
tasks: Check and organise financial information.
Prepare reports and explain what the numbers mean.
Identify financial risks or ways to improve operations.
route: Explore accounting or related study and investigate professional qualifications relevant to your country and chosen specialism.
activity: Create a fictional budget for a school club. Record income and expenses in a spreadsheet and explain one trade-off.
question: What could a set of numbers reveal about a business?

title: Biomedical engineer
summary: Connect engineering with biology to develop and improve technology used in healthcare.
tasks: Design or test medical technology and equipment.
Work with clinicians to understand a healthcare need.
Check performance, document findings and improve designs.
route: Explore biomedical engineering or a related engineering degree. Look for design projects and placements in healthcare technology.
activity: Sketch a device that makes an everyday task more accessible. Label the user’s need and three design features.
question: How would you find out whether a design really helps its user?

title: Data scientist
summary: Find patterns in data and turn them into explanations, predictions and better decisions.
tasks: Find useful data and organise it for analysis.
Build and test statistical or computational models.
Use charts and clear explanations to share findings.
route: Explore mathematics, statistics, computing or related study. Practise analysing real datasets and explaining both results and limitations.
activity: Use a public weather dataset to make one chart. Write down what it shows and one thing it cannot tell you.
question: What evidence would make you change your first conclusion?

title: Physiotherapist
summary: Help people improve movement and function through assessment, rehabilitation and education.
tasks: Assess a person’s movement and discuss their goals.
Develop and adapt a rehabilitation plan.
Track progress and explain the recovery process.
route: Explore an approved physiotherapy or physical therapy programme, clinical placements and local licensing. The degree route varies by country.
activity: Research a physiotherapy setting, such as a sports clinic or hospital. Make a short poster about the professional’s role.
question: Why might two people with similar injuries need different goals?

title: Psychologist
summary: Study how people think, feel and behave, and use evidence to understand human experiences.
tasks: Ask research questions and gather evidence about behaviour.
Analyse patterns and explain findings.
Work in a chosen specialism, such as research, education or clinical practice.
route: Explore psychology study and the further training required for your intended specialism. Many psychologist roles require advanced study and registration.
activity: Read about one published psychology experiment. Identify its research question and one limitation, without testing or diagnosing anyone.
question: How could you investigate a question about behaviour fairly?

title: Film & video editor
summary: Shape raw footage into a story through pacing, sequencing, sound and visual choices.
tasks: Review footage and choose material for a story.
Arrange scenes, sound and transitions.
Work with a director or team to refine the final edit.
route: Explore film, media or related training and make a portfolio of short edits. Practise storytelling alongside editing software.
activity: Edit the same five clips into two short sequences: one calm and one exciting. Use your own or openly licensed footage.
question: How can the order of two shots change their meaning?

title: Market research analyst
summary: Investigate what people need and want, helping organisations make better product decisions.
tasks: Plan ways to gather useful customer information.
Study responses, competitors and market patterns.
Present findings and explain what they could mean for a business.
route: Explore business, communications, social science or related study. Build research and statistics skills through small projects.
activity: Ask five volunteers which school-club activity they prefer. Make an anonymous tally and explain why five answers may not represent everyone.
question: What would you ask before creating a product for someone else?

title: Lawyer
summary: Research legal questions, explain rights and responsibilities, and represent clients’ interests.
tasks: Listen to a client and investigate the facts.
Research legal issues and prepare documents.
Explain options or present an argument on a client’s behalf.
route: Research the law degree or conversion route, professional training and admission rules in the jurisdiction where you want to practise.
activity: Prepare both sides of a friendly debate about a school rule. Separate facts, opinions and assumptions.
question: Can you explain the strongest argument against your own position?

title: Electrician
summary: Install, maintain and troubleshoot the electrical systems that power homes and workplaces.
tasks: Interpret technical diagrams and plan work.
Install or maintain electrical systems.
Test equipment and identify faults using approved procedures.
route: Explore an apprenticeship or technical training route with supervised practical experience. Check local qualification and licensing requirements.
activity: Use a virtual circuit simulator to connect a battery, switch and lamp. Explain what happens when the switch opens.
question: How would you approach a fault methodically rather than guessing?

title: Chef
summary: Combine creativity, technique and teamwork to plan dishes and lead the preparation of food.
tasks: Develop recipes, menus and food presentation.
Coordinate a kitchen team and ingredients.
Maintain food quality, hygiene and safe working practices.
route: Explore culinary training, apprenticeships or supervised kitchen experience. Leadership roles usually build on practical experience.
activity: Plan a three-dish menu on a budget. Calculate ingredient costs and explain how you would avoid waste.
question: How would you balance taste, cost and the needs of different diners?

title: Agricultural & food scientist
summary: Investigate ways to grow food, care for resources and improve the quality of what we eat.
tasks: Research crops, soils, animals or food production.
Compare results from field or laboratory work.
Share findings that could improve quality, safety or resource use.
route: Explore agricultural, food, plant or related sciences. Seek field or laboratory projects; some research roles need further study.
activity: Grow two sets of seeds under different light conditions. Keep other conditions similar and record growth over a week.
question: How would you make the comparison a fair test?

title: Environmental scientist
summary: Use evidence to understand environmental problems and help protect people and ecosystems.
tasks: Plan investigations and collect environmental information.
Analyse data to understand a problem.
Recommend actions and explain the evidence to others.
route: Explore environmental or other natural sciences and build fieldwork, data and report-writing skills. Requirements depend on the role.
activity: Observe litter in a safe public area without handling it. Record categories and propose one change to reduce it.
question: What evidence would show whether your proposed change worked?

title: Pilot
summary: Plan and operate flights, using careful preparation, teamwork and navigation to move people or cargo.
tasks: Check flight plans, aircraft information and weather.
Coordinate with crew and air traffic control.
Operate and monitor the aircraft throughout a flight.
route: Research approved flight training, medical standards, licences and experience requirements with your country’s aviation regulator. Routes differ for commercial and airline roles.
activity: Draw a route between two cities. Use a map scale to estimate distance, then research how weather might affect planning.
question: Why is preparation as important as controlling the aircraft?
